headline: The clap test breathes again on Chrome 157
lede: Headless Chrome 157 silenced the synth-mic trick every voice suite used for two months — zero recorded chunks, no error. The witness path now feeds Chrome's own fake capture device from a baked WAV: real recorder, real opus, real upload, claps returning at baked+17.6 ms with 0.2 ms spread. Every run stamps where its audio came from.

notes.text: #2716: fakemic library + plaicraft-clap and voicedrive migrated to fake-file capture; correct --use-fake-device-for-media-stream spelling (the old -for-media-capture suffix matched no flag at all).

npm run micprobe — a permanent capture-shape battery: it prints the Chrome version and what each input shape delivers, so the next engine break gets named by a check instead of rediscovered through twenty red suite lines.

Under cross-lane load the recorder starves honestly now: takes upload with audio:false, and the clap driver SKIPs time-shaped gates with the measured fps rather than accusing the game. A --witness run still never skips.
claptestplay migration stays on #2709 — several clap schedules share one browser today; one fake file serves one schedule.

look.text: Play Gauntlet — the auto-capture path this work keeps honest
